title: Reach and dissemination channels of (selected) disinformation narratives in Serbia
screen_reason: Survey of 800 Serbian internet users (7-27 June 2023) asked, for each of seven fact-checked false narratives, whether the respondent had heard it before. The share answering yes ranges from 37.13% (Pentagon biolabs) to 85.13% (COVID-19 created by the West). These are RECALL exposure shares with a population denominator. Belief/agreement with the narratives is also reported but is excluded by the belief rule.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (a) agreement/belief with each narrative (21.75% N1 to 49.00% N4) - belief in false claims is explicitly excluded; (b) Table 2, the distribution of channels through which respondents heard each narrative (press, radio, TV, digital, social media, each row summing to about 100) - this is a breakdown of where those who heard it heard it, not a share of content or of the population exposed to misinformation, and its denominator is the mentions of those who heard the narrative, not the 800; (c) figures the paper cites from other studies (6% of news diet, 0.15% of daily media diet, 33% BuzzFeed/Ipsos, 11.5% German election, 85% of Serbian citizens having encountered fake news in a cited Reuters/other study, 14% false recall) - all barred by R8 as figures cited from elsewhere. Discrepancies worth a human's attention: (1) the text says 'Three least heard narratives (N1-N3) are those describing the relations between Russia and the EU/USA', but N3 has the second-HIGHEST reach in both Figure 1 and Figure 3 (77.4%); the three lowest are in fact N2 (37.1), N1 (44.8) and N4 (48.1), so the sentence looks like an error. (2) The method section says 'each participant was presented with a disinformation narrative from Table 1' (singular), which would imply about 114 respondents per narrative, but every reported percentage in Figures 1-3 is an exact multiple of 1/800 (e.g. 21.75 = 174/800, 85.13 = 681/800, 37.13 = 297/800), so all 800 respondents evidently answered about all seven narratives; I coded the denominator as 800 on that arithmetic. (3) The values had to be read off bar-chart labels because the figures are images with scattered text labels; the two figures agree with each other, which is why confidence is still high.

rob.design: Two-phase design. Phase 1: 25 fact-checked false claims collected from three Serbian fact-checking portals (Istinomer, AFP Fact Check, Fake News Tragac) between 10 and 28 April 2023, from which seven narratives were selected as representatives of five meta-narratives. Phase 2: self-administered online survey by the GESOP agency, 7-27 June 2023, N=800 aged 18-74, interlocked quotas by sex, age and zone of residence, margin of error +/- 3.5%; the authors note the online-only mode and the absence of an education quota lower representativeness. Reach measured by a binary yes/no recall item per narrative; belief measured on a 1-8 scale aggregated to three categories. No response rate reported; no coder reliability applicable.
rob.item6_quote: Disinformation is most frequently defined as deliberately falsified information that is intended to cause harm to a person, social group or entire country (Wardle and Derakhshan 2017).
rob.item10_quote: The results obtained through the survey show that four out of seven narratives have been heard by more than half of the respondents, with even the least heard narrative (N2) still reaching a third of the survey population (Figure 1).
